fieldsRead.programmeDescription: International Business Administration studies how organisations operate across borders and respond to economic, social and environmental change. It combines management, marketing, finance and organisational research with responsible enterprise.
fieldsRead.comparisonExplanation: The published curriculum allocates 180 EC, but its thesis-entry rules disagree about the required credits and earlier methods courses. Relevant UCR programmes have been assessed provisionally. A final comparison is withheld until the applicable entry rule can be established.

curriculum.limitation: The allocation is 150 EC of required study and 30 EC of open study. It is not yet a fully verified degree pathway. The adopted regulations require 90 programme EC and older named methods courses for thesis entry; the current thesis description instead requires 102 EC and names Academic Skills, Quantitative Methods 1 and Sustainable Entrepreneurship. Their application to the renewed curriculum needs clarification.

It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

preparedDescriptions.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
